scope: Local DSR runs on candidate working trees. Each source field gives the commit, tracked-diff digest and untracked-files digest. Training quality and runtime results apply to the measured configurations.

Two RTX 4090s, D1 bio_all reference, 91,165,440 parameters, 65,536 tokens/update. The 0.40 GPU-hour watchdog stopped training before any completed update or checkpoint. Charged elapsed 732.11191 seconds × 2, exit 137
Both nightly jobs passed including the full master battery, perf, real eight-cell pipeline and uncertainty; DSR invalidated the run because the shared registry changed while it ran
Two real Gloo ranks each read 16 B8×T1024 CPU batches from train and validation. Distinct rank input hashes. 54,511.6 train and 37,640.8 validation positions/s aggregate; host input only
Counterexample against old watchdog: TERM-resistant job consumed 20.139 seconds of a 10-second allocation; test failed as expected
16 performance/repetition tests passed; Ruff, ty and UBS passed on the candidate
Same step-50 synaptic checkpoint, 4 calibration and 16 independent validation documents: fewer greedy repeated trigrams, zero sampled repeats in both arms, NLL interval spans zero
Eight independently trained binding models produced original calibration and test traces. The data-generating job passed; a subsequent type check failed
Four direct tests, independent re-derivation over original 1,024 labelled rows, Ruff, ty and UBS passed. Registered advantages not observed
Final DSR runner shell syntax and UBS passed on the Mac dispatcher

Linux local DSR main rebuilt Rust and verified its signed scanner, then the locked CPU type checker rejected a dict-expanded scalar_lr in the optimizer factory. Superseded by an explicitly typed call.

Standing DSR nightly on the locked CPU image. The validation battery passed, and uncertainty passed. The separate cost gate measured standard/synaptic 1.91x for training and 1.67x for cached decode against limits 2.00x and 1.50x; the nightly correctly failed.

Corrected launcher and scoring watchdogs: 43 matrix cases pass, including termination inside the allocation, delayed score refusal and refusal to resume an overdrawn ledger. Whole-tree ruff/ty pass and scoped UBS has zero critical findings.

After source-specific requalification the mapped suite passed 288 with 3 environment skips across 291 tests. All 19 compiled Lean declarations passed the explicit axiom allowlist. This verifies the reduced-model mapping and regressions.
Installed the frozen CUDA Python environment and built the project Rust extension on the dual-4090 worker. Each downstream check has its own exit in this preparation receipt.
The shared bare pytest launcher selected an interpreter missing Torch. The timer source passed lint, type checks and scoped UBS; the runtime retry used the environment interpreter.
The optimizer-boundary timing regression passed using python -m pytest. Fourteen of 15 performance tests passed. The real relative CPU training gate failed at 2.44x vs 2.00x under this worker load.

Exploratory native_presyn=1 reached both D1 updates, validated at step 2 and committed both rank shards in 410.199 s / 0.22789 GPUh. Training exit 0. The outer DSR receipt was invalidated when the trainer appended the default tracked registry. Only that registry changed; source-stable replay would be needed to qualify this observation.

The standalone registered-preset scorer refused this exploratory checkpoint because native_presyn differs from bio_all. The mismatch guard remains intact. The saved-config base_loss entry point is the appropriate independent measurement.
Completed 16 trained MoE cells across four paired training seeds. A test-only type issue failed the initial DSR envelope; outcomes and raw traces were retained.
The prerequisite-matched four-seed MoE experiment passed 5 tests, lint, typing and UBS. The 95% paired bootstrap interval lay within ±0.01 nats on the held-out synthetic task.

Standing DSR main rebuilt the wheel and passed Rust fmt/clippy/tests. The corrected optimizer call eliminated the old type error. The separate floating uvx type checker failed on warnings in multiple modules, while the project-locked CPU tool was independently checked.

Saved-config standalone loss evaluation reloaded the exploratory step-2 checkpoint, scored 1,048,576 FineWeb positions per split, then generated samples in 376.58 s on one RTX 4090. Train BPB 5.1592, held-out BPB 5.3024.

First measured hardware baseline, followed by an independent replay on the same RTX 4090. Four absolute checks passed. Training slowdown 1.37x passed, cached decode 2.43x exceeded 1.50x and correctly made this DSR run fail. Shell checks passed.

Quick Start trained a real tiny bio checkpoint and the validation-only command returned finite BPB for 128 held-out positions. Ruff and locked ty passed. UBS reported two critical findings in the original code path, leaving this DSR run red.
326 scoped CPU regression cases passed across the nine type repairs.
Fourteen end-to-end Quick Start and matrix tests passed on the nine-file type repair.
Whole-tree DSR on the type repair reached UBS: 9 critical and 26 warnings over 378 files. The strict resource-lifecycle gate remained red.
The unfiltered precommit scanner completed on the nine repaired files with zero critical findings, 55 warnings and 417 notes.
In the original locked CPU container both ty 0.0.75 and ty 0.0.108 passed the full tree with the nine fixes and the validation-only candidate. Ruff and clean-diff checks passed.
Data-only legacy tokenizer with 18/18 direct cases, Ruff and ty passed, scoped UBS 0 critical and 4 warnings.
Native tiny training followed by validation-only checkpoint reload and scoring of 128 positions passed, Ruff and ty passed, scoped UBS 0 critical and 4 warnings.

Canonical hardware job passed 9/9 CUDA and 61/61 reference/Rust tests, both same-invocation fused speedups and 4/4 absolute drift gates. Failed relative vs vanilla for train (2.29x vs 2.00x) and cached decode (2.34x vs 1.50x).

Before the Hebbian repair 25/36 synthetic continual fits completed, with zero complete bio-sleep pairs. Gauge and EWC produced identical final weights in all six seeds. Replay preserved A but missed B acquisition. DSR passed the frozen reporter checks and retained failed scientific arms.
Pre-rebinding the live formal manifest correctly rejected the changed synaptic.py. The reported new hash was 6357b25cf14a145df46d5b77db4c9fe6028983b8b86d66cae45871ec8c27f10b.

Four release-current curves, six live molecular fast-weight reconstruction points and an intentionally out-of-domain Bernoulli test: 7/7 tests passed. Ruff, ty and UBS passed (0 critical, 0 warnings).
Whole changed-file UBS remains red at the trusted config executor. Standing and scoped checks retained; no scanner rules were suppressed.
Both locked and floating ty, whole-repo Ruff and post-Ruff clean diff passed.
Direct entry-point, type-override, JSON and validation-only checkpoint regressions passed; CPU Flex availability is a separate environment condition.
Strict UBS still fails on 2 intentional executable Python boundaries and 17 exact-type schema checks across 378 files. Eight prior findings removed without changing the scanner.

Corrected normalized Hebbian path passed 67 direct tests and completed 36/36 unchanged continual cells. All 24 unaffected final weights matched. Sleep and both controls each retained zero A targets out of 768; paired differences zero.
The old Hebbian implementation failed 4 of 5 prospective numerical/atomicity regression cases, including matrix and norm overflow; small input passed.

Two-GPU 24-step vanilla pilot processed 6,291,456 tokens and independently scored 3.19468229 BPB on 1,048,576 held-out targets. Frozen 1,900-step projection 23,579.64 s exceeded 12,570 s training limit. Full run declined.

Standing main DSR on published 8f49e72 failed its strict Python quality stage. Rust and wheel stages succeeded. Later repairs were tested separately and two executable-Python boundaries and 17 schema checks still flag under strict UBS.

Eight trained variable-binding models, 256 paired prompts. Single pass 29/256 correct, actual correction 14/256 with 115 abstentions, zero initial errors rescued. 3.139x backbone calls and 3.035x measured time. Full iteration records and 32 direct tests.
Complete CPU suite at the original isolated qualification snapshot: 2,003 passed, 14 failed, 11 skipped in 10,853.78s. Current targeted and full checks are separate.
At the normalized-Hebbian snapshot, 288 mapped tests passed, three skipped and all 19 resolved Lean declarations passed the axiom audit.
Nsight Systems NVTX tracing and SQLite export for two train and two decode windows on a physical RTX 4090.
Four measured timing windows rendered to JSON/SVG; the separate quality command exited 2 in the scanner.
Six attention benchmark tests passed and one skipped; Ruff, ty and the scoped scanner passed.
Original attention tool returned zero even when all five compiled rows failed on Python 3.14. Four eager rows completed at both T128 and T1024.
Corrected RTX4090 CLI: the four requested supported rows exited 0, then the five-row matrix retained all rows and exited 2 on the unsupported Flex path.
Eight paired seeds, diffusion and plain baseline trained on 228 synthetic commands. At 400 steps, 52 versus 87 correct out of 576 per arm.
Checked the study harness and its analytical controls; raw results independently replayed in a separate run.
Independent verifier checked 3456 predictions, 10368 edge observations, exact paired comparisons and all 360 analytic controls.
Counted both complete 249036800-pair rank-local training streams.
Verified smoothed unigram and bigram scores on 5053422 held-out target bytes; full count-model exposure, pilot-only neural exposure.
Verified both physical checkpoint generations and archived training curves, retrieval tests, generated samples and standalone scoring.

Fresh default structural NAS protocol cc21c16f5e99. Sixteen equal-work outcomes and eight paired seeds, all invariants passed. NAS final loss increased 0.003267; the experiment returned its regression status.
Old manifest rejected the exact changed Flex benchmark test digest at 129fb69.

At 129fb69, 11/12 affected cases failed under the shared worker environment, including a wrong global pytest interpreter, 6 deadlines, two stale audit classifications, a missing current structural result, and the normalized readout mismatch.

The real working-memory demo, structural report and matrix column repairs passed. Of 32 selected tests the remaining first-pass failure was the new real core import of configurator; Ruff and ty passed.
After switching to project-interpreter pytest the nested runner loaded Torch; on the shared filesystem it reached its existing 45-second timeout.
CPU live performance exceeded its fixed threshold; separate source and type checks passed. See per-check log hashes.

Standing one-command Nsight capture, SQLite export and JSON/SVG render succeeded. All four CUDA launch counts exactly reproduced the first atlas: 1145/2150 in five training steps and 15000/24800 in 200 cached tokens.

Unshipped FP32 cached RoPE/RMS candidate. All 90 primitive cases, 156 token logits/argmax and 36 KV steps passed. Twelve balanced same-GPU rounds: median candidate/incumbent 1.1066x, paired 95% bootstrap 0.8735–1.2644. Failed prespecified lower bound; vanilla/candidate median 2.2467x.

Second Linux worker, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu and native ABI 1: all 40 selected tests passed. Distributed AdamW/Muon, child termination, CPU Triton interpreter, normalized working-memory head, actual NAS report, matrix controls, reviewed footprint and validation subprocess retained their original bounds.
Repository-wide Ruff and the installed locked ty both passed on the second Linux worker.
Fresh Darwin arm64 CPU extra with Python 3.14.6: the original frozen project requested Triton, which had no compatible Darwin wheel.
Repaired manifest and lock validated (137 packages). Native CPU dry-run selected the Darwin Torch wheel and omitted Triton. Cold offline installation lacked the Torch archive.

Installed the full CPU+dev project into a new native macOS arm64 Python 3.14.6 environment. Offline wheel input used 91 archives matched by lockfile hash, including the project build backend. Cargo fetched missing pinned inputs with the project user-agent.
Native ABI 1 and PyTorch 2.9.1 loaded with no Triton installed. All ten end-to-end public Quick Start tests passed on arm64 macOS, including tokenizer, real train, checkpoint validation and chat.
Rechecked published study raw bytes with the independent verifier and matched pilot observations, count numerator and original Nsight SQLite digest.
Original renderer failed both continuously busy, overlapping-kernel controls (7 ns and 101 ns windows). It divided by nominal instead of actual bin widths.

Two independent occupancy counterexamples now pass; rendered the archived trace, and Ruff/ty passed. All scalar fields and kernel/API totals matched; maximum bin change on the recorded trace was 0.000000648 percentage points.
Verified the platform marker with the universal lock. Linux CPU resolved the same 92 external distributions before and after; GPU the same 107, including pinned Triton 3.5.1 on both.
Final Flex test binding: 288 mapped tests passed, three skipped, compiled Lean audit verified all 19 resolved theorem identities against allowed axioms.

Full independent CPU qualification on 129fb69 with the working-memory, global pytest, current NAS report, package boundary and matrix repairs: 2063 passed, 11 skipped and 1 failed in 678.87s. Live training measured 5305.4 vs 10863.7 tok/s (2.05x vs the 2.00x limit).

First 6291456 true optimizer pairs, same two independently hashed rank prefixes; same 1048576 validation positions and 5053422 target bytes. Vanilla 3.1946823 BPB, unigram 2.3321287, smoothed bigram 2.2341526. Grouped and per-observation bit numerators agreed.
Intentionally stopped a duplicate shared-GPU-worker CPU suite after its checkout was superseded and the independent 2075-test Linux run completed. Exit 143 is not a completed suite.
All six changed Python files, including the corrected atlas, completed the signed per-file scanner with zero critical findings.
Scoped UBS ran all six changed Python files together. The scanner completed with zero critical findings, 15 warnings and 50 informational findings.

The post-atlas Linux CPU suite exercised 2077 cases: 2065 passed, 11 skipped and one failed in 711.14s. The only failure measured 4643.1 synaptic vs 9669.2 vanilla train tokens/s, a 2.08x slowdown at the unchanged 2.00x limit.

First checkpoint-precision harness incorrectly promoted nonpersistent rotary buffers. Vanilla rejected the invalid dtype, the bio arm completed and the static check ran. No format decision uses these measurements.

The public CUDA chat CLI loaded the real step-24 vanilla checkpoint and completed one selective-decode prompt with --dtype float32. It reported predictive entropy 8.77 nats against the deliberate 0.01 threshold.

With original checkpoint-loader buffers preserved, both four-mode RTX 4090 cohorts completed all 40 trials including warmups. Across the 64 measured cached positions TF32 recovered 64 greedy reference tokens, BF16 zero, and FP16 two. None met the registered speed-and-fidelity rule. Full raw per-format data are versioned.

Independent forward hooks reconstructed all 128 vanilla cached choices across the four formats. Widening only the final softcap in the saved BF16 and FP16 head traces restored all 32 highest-FP32 greedy decisions in each arm. Original BF16 maxima tied across 289 to 468 tokens, and FP16 maxima tied across 72 to 90.
Both unmodified GPT heads failed the BF16 and FP16 near-saturation ordering witness, all four cases. The original rounded scores made the first two distinct matrix outputs exactly equal.

Whole-project Ruff and ty passed; all 63 head, checkpoint and deliberation cases passed against the repaired inference formula; UBS on all five touched Python files completed with zero critical or warning findings.

On the real vanilla checkpoint at prompt length 1024, widening the head with ordinary tensor temporaries increased peak allocation above the inputs and weights from 531784704 bytes to 934437888. Both observed full-output dtypes and T32 results were retained, motivating a same-result buffer reuse probe.

At the first corrected head implementation the full CPU run exercised 2081 cases in 700.27s: 2069 passed, 11 skipped and one failed the 2.00x live training limit at 5078.1 versus 10670.9 tokens/s (2.10x).

Four full sweeps on the widened inference heads, sampling the original and disjoint subsequent stream blocks on both real checkpoints. BF16, FP16 and TF32 each matched the FP32 decision on 128/128 measured positions. All original 40 scalar training losses were exactly reproduced. No timing cohort met the registered joint speed rule.

Against the live full prefill, last-position vocabulary projection matched KV, biological cache state and the greedy choice for all four checkpoint/length cases. Nevertheless 31/33 vanilla and 18/23 synaptic final logits exceeded atol=rtol=1e-5 at T32/T1024 respectively out of 65536 logits per case. Lower memory did not qualify the candidate.

The allocation-preserving serving implementation and its differentiable training-free head path passed whole-project Ruff/ty, all 63 focused tests and UBS with zero warning/critical findings. The four lower-precision witnesses checked exact equality of autograd and inference results plus finite, nonzero selected weight gradients.
On native macOS arm64, the serving implementation passed the full 14-case head suite and all ten real Quick Start tests, 24/24 in 70.67s. DSR Ruff --fix completed without changes.

Within one DSR invocation, the revised FP32 serving buffer and the original FP32 expression produced identical SHA-256 for every output score at T32 and T1024, covering 2097152 and 67108864 values. T1024 reduced incremental peak from 934437888 to 531784704 bytes (384 MiB), equal to the old low-precision head. T32 saved 11.625 MiB.

Final serving implementation with buffer reuse: full Linux CPU suite 2069 passed, 11 skipped and one failed in 700.37s across 2081 cases. The unchanged live training budget measured 5017.7 synaptic versus 11176.1 vanilla tokens/s, a 2.23x slowdown against 2.00x.

The unmodified public Engine.generate ran 16 autoregressive tokens on two further real validation prompts per checkpoint. Original BF16 and FP16 each agreed with FP32 at 0/64 aligned positions, whereas repaired BF16 and FP16 each agreed at 64/64 and matched all four complete sequences. All four reference sequences repeated one token, so this is precision fidelity, not chat quality.

fused_feasibility.interpretation: The configured kernel produced a complete checkpoint and the saved model scored held-out text. These two updates supply no registered D1 quality comparison or sustained throughput estimate.
